overview: The D435i is what a stereo camera becomes once you add a dedicated depth-processing ASIC and an IMU: two IR imagers plus an IR dot projector give it active stereo vision that works even on plain, texture-less walls, and the onboard vision processor turns that into a finished depth image at up to 90fps without ever loading the host CPU. The 'i' specifically means it has a built-in Bosch BMI055 6-axis IMU, hardware-timestamped and aligned to the depth/color frames, which is what makes visual-inertial SLAM (tracking camera motion, not just scene depth) possible without a second sensor. Unlike the catalog's other cameras, it hands you three synchronized data streams at once — RGB, depth, and IMU — over a single USB-C cable, which is exactly why it needs real USB3 bandwidth and a real host computer, not a microcontroller.
simpleSummary: A camera that sees full 3D depth at every pixel and also senses its own motion, instead of just taking flat pictures.

specifications.depthTechnology: Active IR stereo (dual IR imagers + IR dot projector)
specifications.onboardIMU: Bosch BMI055, 6-DOF accel+gyro, hardware-synced to depth/RGB frames

pinMap.name: USB-C
pinMap.function: Single USB-C 3.1 connector carrying bus power plus the RGB stream, stereo depth stream, and IMU stream simultaneously.
pinMap.currentLimit: ~700mA-1A sustained, higher transient at stream startup
pinMap.gotcha: Needs a genuine USB3 port and cable. Plugging into a USB2 port or an unpowered USB2 hub still 'works' but silently caps bandwidth, forcing lower resolution/frame rate or dropping the RGB stream entirely with no obvious error.

useCases.title: Bin-picking robotic arm
useCases.scenario: Generate a dense point cloud of a cluttered parts bin so a grasp-planning algorithm can pick a specific object's pose, not just its 2D silhouette.

useCases.title: Visual-inertial SLAM
useCases.scenario: Fuse the depth stream with the onboard IMU (via RTAB-Map or ORB-SLAM3) to map an environment and track camera motion without relying on wheel odometry.

useCases.title: Dense obstacle avoidance
useCases.scenario: Treat the whole depth frame as a proximity field for a mobile robot, catching obstacles at any height in the frame instead of a single ultrasonic ping straight ahead.

useCases.title: Hand/gesture tracking for human-robot interaction
useCases.scenario: Use the depth stream to segment and track a hand or body skeleton for gesture-based robot control.

useCases.title: 3D object scanning
useCases.scenario: Sweep the camera around a small object and fuse successive depth frames into a 3D mesh for reverse-engineering or 3D printing.

oftenConfusedWith: HC-SR04 (a single distance number vs. a full grid of distance readings, one per pixel, ~30 times a second)

Stereo Camera Module (looks similar with two lenses, but a raw stereo module has no onboard depth ASIC or IR projector — it hands you two raw video feeds and leaves depth computation to your own CPU/GPU)
OV7670/USB Webcam (RGB image only, no depth channel at all)
oftenUpgradedTo: Industrial structured-light 3D scanners for sub-millimeter static scan accuracy
3D LiDAR (Spinning) when the required sensing range exceeds the D435i's ~10m limit or full 360° coverage is needed

beginnerMistakes: Using a USB2 cable or an unpowered hub, which chokes bandwidth without throwing a clear error.
Running it outdoors in direct sunlight, where the IR projector's dot pattern gets washed out and active stereo depth degrades badly.
Forgetting the ~10.5cm minimum depth range — objects closer than that fall into a blind zone with no reading.
Assuming the IMU stream is enabled by default — most librealsense examples need it explicitly turned on in the stream configuration.
Powering it from an underpowered USB port (some phone chargers/hubs), causing random stream dropouts during heavy depth processing.
